summary: Pascale Hugon is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She taught Flavio A. Geisshuesler and held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania. In 2012, she was attested as a professor at Thammasat University.

Patrice Ladwig works in Buddhist and religious studies, having studied at the University of Münster, University of Edinburgh, and EHESS. He held posts at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

Patricia Berger, a scholar of art history, Buddhist studies, and sinology, earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley under Steven D. Goodman and Mark Elliott. She served as Curator at the Asian Art Museum and joined UC Berkeley's faculty in 1996.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and sinologist who studied at the University of Chicago and Columbia University. She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1982), the Institute for Advanced Study (1998), and the University of Washington (1997–2020).

Patricia Fister is a scholar of Japanology, art history, and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. from the University of Kansas (~1978–1983). She taught at the University of Kansas (~1985–1991) and was a professor at Nichibunken (~1991–2019).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a sinologist and Tibetologist. She completed graduate study at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.
Patrick Arthur Pranke is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis O. Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.

Patrick McAllister is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2004–2011) under Helmut Krasser, Karin Preisendanz, and Ernst Steinkellner.

Patrick Olivelle, an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied at Oxford (~1968–1972) and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1974) under Ludo Rocher. He held posts at Indiana University (1974–1991) and UT Austin (from 1991).
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied as a Ph.D. candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles, under Robert E. Buswell Jr. (attested 2012).

Patrul Rinpoche (1808–1887) was a master of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu (~1830) and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught Zhenphen Chokyi Nangwa and Shechen Gyaltsab, among others.

Pattaratorn Chirapravati is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell. She held posts at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco and California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016).

Paul B. Donnelly works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa (attested 1997), Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe, and Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Bernard (1929–2015) was an archaeologist of Central Asia and the Hellenized East. Educated at the ENS and Sorbonne, he directed the DAFA (1965–1980) and held posts at the CNRS (1973) and the EPHE (1981).

Paul Carus (1852–1919) was a philosopher and scholar of religion and Buddhist studies. After studying at Greifswald, Strasbourg, and Tübingen (Ph.D. ~1875–1876), he taught at Kriegsschule Dresden and worked at Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919).

Paul Copp is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religion. He studied at UMass Amherst and Princeton (Ph.D. attested 2005) under Stephen F. Teiser, and held posts at the Heidelberg Academy, Western Michigan University, and the University of Chicago.
Paul Courtright is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and Emory University (attested 1998).

Paul Crowe is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. He pursued graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and served as a professor at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

Paul David Devanandan (1901–1962) was a religious studies and Indology scholar educated at Nizam College, Presidency College, and Yale (doctorate ~1927–1931). He served at United Theological College (1932–1949) and directed the CISRS (1956).
